fieldMarks: Very large, 64-86 cm, and mostly black
White wing patches obvious in flight, not when swimming
Male larger and glossier than female, with a knob above the bill
Domesticated forms usually have much white in the plumage
behavior: Wild birds are wary, fast-flying birds of wooded rivers and swamps
Nests in tree cavities and will use nest boxes
Not often heard; quiet quacks and grunts
habitat: Wooded rivers and swamps in the wild; domestic-type birds around ponds and urban and suburban waters.
range: Wild birds are native from northeastern Mexico south to South America, with small numbers on the Rio Grande in southern Texas. Most Muscovies in North America are barnyard-type birds, and U.S. records probably pertain to escapes or unsuccessful introductions (NatureServe).
